newsitem.title: USA: Nobel prize winner sentenced for sexual abuse.
newsitem.headline: Nobel prize winner sentenced for sexual abuse.

text.p: A Nobel Prize winning research scientist was sentenced on Tuesday to 18 months in prison for sexually abusing a teenage boy he brought back with him from one of his research trips in Micronesia.

Daniel Carleton Gajdusek, 74, who won the 1976 Nobel Prize in medicine, is now in state prison, States Attorney Scott Rolle said. Judge Edward Dwyer agreed to a plea bargain reached by the researcher in February and merged two 15-year sentences into one. Then he suspended all but 18 months.

Gajdusek won the prize for his study of the transmission of viruses related to neurological disorders. He was also involved in recent research into development of a test for Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease, the human form of mad cow disease.
Rolle said Gajdusek brought scores of young men back from his researches in Micronesia. "He didn't abuse all the boys, just a few," Rolle said.
Gajdusek defended his actions as being within Micronesian cultural norms for expressing affection but did not attempt that defence in court, Rolle said.

Gajdusek, who retired in February from the National Institutes of Health in Bethesda, Maryland, will be sent to a prison hospital for evaluation, Rolle said. Then he will serve his time in the general inmate population.
